summary: 1933 L-4 lookout replacing a 1917 cupola cabin, famous as the post where poets Gary Snyder and Philip Whalen worked in the 1950s.

facts.design: L-4 groundhouse, 14.25 ft square, rock foundation, shiplap siding, wood-shingled hip roof, diagonally braced plywood shutters

staffing.status: staffed intermittently/every summer per lookout association sources

access.note: North Cascades National Park, reached by approx. 5-mile trail; not a rental, visited frequently by hikers

visit.trail_note: about 5 miles from trailhead to the cabin

events.note: original cupola-style lookout cabin built under Mt. Baker National Forest
1917 cupola torn down and replaced with current L-4 groundhouse, built by the CCC
transferred from Forest Service to National Park Service when North Cascades National Park was created by Congress
poet Gary Snyder staffed the lookout summer 1953, inspiring two of his poems
poet Philip Whalen staffed the lookout after Snyder was not rehired; wrote poem 'Sourdough Mountain Lookout'
wrapped in fire-proof material in August 2023 due to the nearby Sourdough Fire

evidence.supports: built 1933 on Mt Baker NF, transferred to NPS 1967, L-4 replaced 1917 cupola, popular hike, continues in active service
evidence.quote: Sourdough Mountain lookout was built on the Mt. Baker National Forest in 1933 and transferred to the National Park Service when the North Cascades National Park was created by Congress in 1967. The L-4 groundhouse replaced a cupola lookout dating to 1917. A popular hiking destination, the lookout continues in active service.

evidence.supports: built by CCC 1933, NRHP 1989, earlier 1917 lookout torn down, structure dimensions and materials, 5 mile hike, Snyder and Whalen tenures and poems, 2023 fire wrap
evidence.quote: An earlier lookout was erected at the site in 1917 but was torn down when the current lookout was constructed. The current structure was built atop a rock foundation and is 14.25 ft (4.34 m) by 14.25 ft (4.34 m) square.

evidence.supports: 1917 cupola developed, present L-4 built 1933, NHLR listed, staffed every summer, location 2 miles NE of Ross Dam, Whatcom County
evidence.quote: Developed in 1917 with a cupola cabin, the present L-4 ground cab was built in 1933 and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register. It is staffed every summer.

corrections.proposed: 1933 (current L-4 structure); 1917 was an earlier, since-replaced cupola cabin
corrections.why: All three sources agree the structure standing today dates to 1933, built by the CCC to replace the 1917 cupola cabin, which was torn down.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Brief's 1917 date refers to the original cupola lookout on the site; the current L-4 groundhouse was built in 1933 after the 1917 structure was demolished. NHLR, Wikipedia, and firelookout.com all agree on this sequence.

notes_for_editor: Built-year conflict resolved: 1917 cupola was replaced by the 1933 L-4 now standing; brief record's 1917 'built' event should probably be relabeled or a 1933 'rebuilt/replaced' event added. Did not verify current staffing status beyond what NHLR/firelookout.com state.
